Command: A Parapet for a New House Roof
Summary: When thou buildest a new house, then thou shalt make a battlement for thy roof, that thou bring not blood upon thine house, if any man fall from thence. This is the biblical root of the duty of care for safety in building.
Commandment: When you build a new house, make a parapet for your roof, so you do not bring bloodguilt on your house.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as civil. The form is ancient — a flat roof used as living space needed a guard — but the duty is timeless: whoever builds something others will use must guard against foreseeable harm, and bears bloodguilt if they do not. Modern building safety law is the same duty in new forms.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: that thou bring not blood upon thine house, if any man fall from thence (Deuteronomy 22:8).
